```text
==================== #101 Subscribe to private repository calendar feeds with a revocable calendar token (comments=0, created 2026-10-22, by vvchopra)
### User Story

Labels: `enhancement`, `scope: medium` · Type: Feature · Part of #36 · Depends on B

## User Story
As a member of a private repository, I want a calendar subscription URL that works without
signing in but only exposes calendar data and can be revoked, so that I can follow private
deadlines in my calendar app without pasting a full-power access token into a third-party service.

### User Scenario

Lena works on the private repo `acme/backend`. On its milestones page she clicks "Subscribe
(iCal)". A dialog explains that the URL contains a personal calendar token and shows
`https://gitea.example/acme/backend/milestones.ics?token=cal_…`. She adds it to Outlook. Later she
pastes the URL by mistake into a shared calendar. She goes to **Settings → Applications →
Calendar token** and clicks "Regenerate", and the old URL stops working at once. When she leaves
the `acme` organization, her feed stops returning `acme/backend` events on its next fetch.


### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1: Given a signed-in user, when they open **Settings → Applications**, then they can
  create, view, regenerate or delete one calendar token. Only a hash is stored, and the plain
  token is shown once, when it is created.
- [ ] AC2: Given a valid calendar token in the `token` query parameter, when it is sent to an
  `.ics` route of a private repo the token owner can read, then the feed is returned with
  `Cache-Control: private`.
- [ ] AC3: Given the same calendar token, when it is sent to any non-`.ics` route (an
  API endpoint, an RSS feed, or a repo page), then it does not authenticate the request.
- [ ] AC4: Given a personal access token, when it is sent as `?token=` to an `.ics` route, then
  it is rejected. Personal access tokens never authenticate calendar feeds.
- [ ] AC5: Given a token whose owner has lost read access to the repository, when the feed is
  fetched, then it returns `404`. Access is checked on every request, not when the token is
  created.
- [ ] AC6: Given a token that has been regenerated or deleted, when the old URL is fetched, then
  it returns `404`.

### Out of Scope

- Tokens limited to one repository, or tokens with expiry dates (possible follow-ups).
- The cross-repository user feed (issue D).
- Admin pages that list or revoke other users' calendar tokens.

### Open Questions

- Should a bad token return `401` or `404`? (Proposed: `404`, so the response does not reveal that
  a private repo exists.)
- Should the token be removed automatica
==================== #102 Subscribe to one personal deadline feed across all my repositories (comments=0, created 2026-10-22, by vvchopra)
### User Story

Labels: `enhancement`, `scope: small` · Type: Feature · Part of #36 · Depends on C

## User Story
As a developer who works across several repositories, I want a single calendar feed of the
deadlines on issues assigned to me and the milestones in my repositories, so that I subscribe
once instead of once per repository.

### User Scenario

Sam is assigned issues in five repositories. Under **Settings → Applications → Calendar token**
he copies the "All my deadlines" URL, `/sam/deadlines.ics?token=cal_…`, and adds it to his
calendar. His assigned issue deadlines from all five repos show up with the repo name in each
title. When he is unassigned from one issue, it drops off the feed on the next refresh.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1: Given a valid calendar token for user `sam`, when `/sam/deadlines.ics?token=…` is
  fetched, then it returns one VEVENT for each open issue with a deadline assigned to `sam` in a
  repository he can read, with titles prefixed by `owner/repo`.
- [ ] AC2: Given a token that belongs to a different user, or no token, when
  `/sam/deadlines.ics` is fetched, then it returns `404`.
- [ ] AC3: Given that Sam loses access to a repository, when the feed is fetched again, then that
  repository's issues are no longer in it.
- [ ] AC4: Given an issue that also appears in that repository's own `issues.ics`, when both
  feeds are compared, then the event has the same `UID` in both, so a client subscribed to both
  feeds shows it once.
- [ ] AC5: Given more matching issues than the cap from issue B, when the feed is fetched, then
  it returns at most the cap.

### Out of Scope

- A cross-repository in-app `/calendar` page (follow-up once A ships).
- Including issues the user created or is watching but is not assigned to.

### Open Questions

- Should milestones of every repository the user can write to be included, or only issues
  assigned to them? (Proposed: assigned issues only, to keep the query bounded.)


### Design Decision

==================== #104 Label picker keeps aria-expanded="true" after Escape closes it (comments=0, created 2026-10-22, by controlled-opposition)
## Observed Behavior
Escape closes the label picker's list in the issue sidebar, but the picker keeps `aria-expanded="true"`. A screen reader announces the picker as expanded while its list is closed.

The picker is a Fomantic dropdown with `role="combobox"`. Gitea's ARIA patch in `web_src/js/modules/fomantic/dropdown.ts` sets its `aria-expanded`.

## Expected Behavior
`aria-expanded` changes to `false` when Escape closes the list, as it does when the picker loses focus.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Sign in, and open an issue in a repository that has at least one label.
2. Press Tab until the **Labels** picker in the sidebar has focus. The list opens.
3. Wait at least 150 ms.
4. Press Escape.
5. Inspect the picker. The list is hidden, focus is still on the picker, and `aria-expanded` is `"true"`.

If you press Escape less than 100 ms after the picker gets focus, `aria-expanded` changes to `"false"`. Step 3 avoids that case.

## Additional Information
- Found on commit `4f8e6ec205` in Chromium and WebKit, through Playwright on macOS.
- Cause, from reading the code: `refreshAriaActiveItem` in `dropdown.ts` sets `aria-expanded`. Only the `focus`, `blur` and `mouseup` listeners and the arrow-key `keyup` listener call it. No listener calls it when Escape closes the list.
- Focusing the picker also fires a `blur` listener, which schedules `refreshAriaActiveItem` 100 ms later. An Escape inside those 100 ms is corrected by that refresh. This hides the bug from a test that presses Escape immediately.
- The test `issue label picker reports collapsed after Escape` in `tests/e2e/multiselect-aria.test.ts` records this bug. It is marked `test.fail()` and links to this issue. When the bug is fixed, the test passes, and Playwright reports it as a failure. Remove the `test.fail()` line in the same PR as the fix.
- Found by #65.

## Design Decision
### Decision 1: refresh the ARIA state when the list hides
**Decision:** Proposed. In `delegateDropdownModule` in `dropdown.ts`, wrap Fomantic's `onHide` setting the same way that function already wraps `onLabelCreate`. The wrapper calls the caller's `onHide`, and then calls `deferredRefreshAriaActiveItem(100)`. The 100 ms delay matches the `blur` listener, which waits for the hide animation. The implementer confirms this approach before the PR.

**Alternatives Considered:**
- (a) Add Escape to the `keyup` listener that refreshes the state on arrow keys.
- (b) Watch the menu's `class` attribute with a `MutationObserver`, and refresh

==================== #36 Calendar view and iCalendar subscription feed (comments=1, created 2026-09-16, by arjunsb26)
### What problem would this solve?

**Summary**
Deadlines in Gitea live only inside Gitea. There is no calendar view, and no way to get dates into the calendar a developer keeps open all day — Gitea publishes RSS and Atom feeds for activity but has no iCalendar support anywhere in the codebase. A team that sets milestone due dates has to re-enter them by hand in Google Calendar or Outlook, and the copies drift the first time a date moves.

**User story**
As a developer, I want my repository's milestones and issue deadlines in the calendar I already use, updating automatically, so that project dates sit alongside the rest of my schedule instead of somewhere I have to remember to check.

**Rough scope — Large**
The calendar view is routine, but private-repository feeds need revocable calendar-scoped tokens in the URL — calendar clients cannot do OAuth — and that security design is the part most likely to expand.

**Source**
Personal use and our team's sprint workflow: we keep milestone dates in Gitea and then maintain them a second time by hand in a shared calendar.

### What do you propose?

**Solution proposal**
A month view inside Gitea plus `.ics` subscription endpoints external calendar apps can follow.

- Calendar view at `/{owner}/{repo}/calendar` showing milestone and issue deadlines, filterable by milestone, assignee, and state; plus a cross-repo `/calendar` for the signed-in user. Build as a Vue component alongside the existing chart components in `web_src/js/components/`.

- Feeds at `/{owner}/{repo}/milestones.ics`, `/{owner}/{repo}/issues.ics`, and `/{user}/deadlines.ics`, served as `text/calendar` with stable `UID`s so moving a date updates the existing event rather than duplicating it. `routers/web/feed/` is the closest precedent for route, permission check, serializer, and content-type.
- **Authentication is the part that needs care.** Calendar clients cannot do OAuth — they fetch a URL on a timer, often with no credential support — which is why this kind of feed is normally a secret URL. Public repos: public feed, matching RSS/Atom. Private repos: a revocable, per-user, **calendar-scoped** token in the URL. It must not reuse personal access tokens, whose scope is far broader and which would then be pasted into third-party services and shared calendars. Feeds must be `Cache-Control: private`.
- Re-check repository access per request, not at token creation, so losing access removes entries from the feed.

### User Story

Labels: `enhancement`, `scope: medium` · Type: Feature · Part of #36
## User Story
As a developer on a repository, I want a month calendar of its milestone due dates and issue
deadlines so that I can see what is due when without scanning the issue list.

### User Scenario

## User Scenario
Priya opens `octo/app` and clicks the new **Calendar** link in the Issues area. She lands on
`/octo/app/calendar`, which shows the current month as a grid. The "Sprint 3" milestone appears on
the 14th, and four issues with deadlines appear on their due days. Each entry shows its title and
links to the milestone or issue. She picks the "Sprint 3" milestone and "assigned to me" in the
filters, and the grid now shows only her Sprint 3 issues. She clicks the next-month arrow, and the
URL updates so she can share that view.

### Acceptance Criteria

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AC1: Given a repository with issues enabled, when a user with read access to issues opens
  `/{owner}/{repo}/calendar`, then a month grid for the current month is shown, with every open
  milestone that has a due date and every issue with a deadline in that month on its due day.
- [ ] AC2: Given an entry on the calendar, when the user clicks it, then they go to that issue or
  milestone page.
- [ ] AC3: Given a milestone, assignee or state (open/closed/all) filter is chosen, when the
  calendar reloads, then only matching issues are shown and the filter values are kept in the
  URL query.
- [ ] AC4: Given the user moves to the previous or next month, when the page reloads, then entries
  for that month are shown and the month is in the URL (`?month=YYYY-MM`).
- [ ] AC5: Given a user without read access to the repository's issues, when they open the
  calendar URL, then they get the same 404 response the issue list gives them.
- [ ] AC6: Given an issue with no deadline (`deadline_unix = 0`), when the calendar is shown, then
  that issue does not appear.

### Out of Scope

## Out of Scope
- `.ics` subscription feeds (issue B, issue C).
- The cross-repository `/calendar` page for the signed-in user (issue D).
- Dragging entries to change a deadline, and week or day views.

## Open Questions

- Where should the Calendar link go: in the issue list header next to Milestones, or as its own
  repository tab?

==================== #100 Subscribe to a public repository's milestones and issue deadlines as an iCalendar feed (comments=0, created 2026-10-22, by vvchopra)
### User Story

Labels: `enhancement`, `scope: medium` · Type: Feature · Part of #36

As a developer, I want to subscribe my calendar app to a public repository's milestone and issue
deadlines so that they appear next to my other events and update when the dates change in Gitea.


### User Scenario

Marco copies `https://gitea.example/octo/app/milestones.ics` and adds it in Google Calendar under
"From URL". Within the client's next refresh, "Sprint 3 (octo/app)" shows on the 14th as an
all-day event. A maintainer moves the milestone to the 21st. On the next refresh the existing
event moves to the 21st instead of a second event being added. He also subscribes to
`issues.ics?state=open` to see open issue deadlines.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1: Given a public repository, when an anonymous client GETs `/{owner}/{repo}/milestones.ics`,
  then the response is `200` with `Content-Type: text/calendar; charset=utf-8` and a valid
  VCALENDAR containing one all-day VEVENT per milestone with a due date.
- [ ] AC2: Given `/{owner}/{repo}/issues.ics`, when fetched, then it contains one all-day VEVENT
  per issue with a deadline (never one for `deadline_unix = 0`), with the issue title, `#index`,
  and a URL to the issue.
- [ ] AC3: Given a milestone or issue whose deadline changes, when the feed is fetched again, then
  the event keeps the same `UID` and has a newer `DTSTAMP`/`SEQUENCE`. A test checks that the UID
  of the same row is the same across two renders with different deadlines.
- [ ] AC4: Given a repository with more issues with deadlines than the cap (proposed 1,000), when
  `issues.ics` is fetched, then the response holds at most the cap, choosing the issues closest to
  today.
- [ ] AC5: Given a private repository, or feeds disabled with `[other] ENABLE_FEED = false`, when
  an anonymous client fetches either `.ics` URL, then it gets `404`, matching the RSS/Atom feeds.
- [ ] AC6: Given the repository's milestone and issue list pages, when viewed, then each shows a
  "Subscribe (iCal)" link to its feed.

### Out of Scope

- Private repositories and any token in the URL (issue C).
- The per-user cross-repository feed (issue D).
- Writing back to Gitea from the calendar (CalDAV).


### Open Questions

- Should the event `UID` use the instance's domain (`issue-{id}@{domain}`)? If so, changing
  `ROOT_URL` would duplicate events in clients that are already subscribed.
- Is 1,000 the right cap, and should it be a setting?

### Design Decision

**Decision
```

````text
# Course workflow — issues, PRs, reviews, sprint deliverables

Course rules, not upstream Gitea ones. Source: the course site <https://csci-435-se.github.io/>
(Sprints pages) and `docs/sprint0/standards.md`. Everyone on the team, and every AI session, uses
the formats below so all issues and PRs look the same. The GitHub templates in `.github/` carry the
same formats; if they ever disagree with this page, fix the template.

AI disclosure has its own page: `AI-ASSISTANCE.md`.

## Current sprint: Sprint 1

- **Dates:** Sep 22 – Oct 8, 2026. Everything pushed and merged by **Oct 8, 11:59 PM**.
- **Points:** 100 (10% of the course grade).
- **Zero rule:** no merged PR (D4), no sprint report (D6) or no release (D7) means **0 for the
  whole sprint**.
- **Carries forward:** every Sprint 0 standard and convention still applies.

| # | Deliverable | Points | Who | Where |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| D1 | Sprint backlog: a `Sprint 1` milestone with every selected issue on it | 10 | Team | GitHub milestone |
| D2 | Requirements spec for each issue (formats below), peer-reviewed by a teammate | 20 | Individual | Issue body |
| D3 | At least one non-trivial design decision per issue | 7 | Individual | Issue body |
| D4 | Code changes and PRs | 36 | Individual | PRs |
| D5 | AI logs | 7 | Individual | `ai-logs/sprint1/<github-username>/` |
| D6 | Sprint report | 10 | Team | `docs/sprint1/report.md` |
| D7 | Release: tag `v1.27.3-csci435-s1` plus a GitHub release | 2 | Team | Tags / Releases |
| D8 | Reflection survey | 8 | Individual | Blackboard/Zulip link |

- **D1 load:** each CSCI 435 student owns at least 2 medium issues; each CSCI 535 student owns at
  least 2 medium and 1 small. Every issue has exactly **one** assignee. Specs should be final by
  Sep 27.
- **D5:** conventions are in `ai-logs/README.md`. The folder must exist even if no AI was used. In
  that case, post an issue comment saying so. Log links go in **issue comments only**, never in PRs
  (`AI-ASSISTANCE.md`).
- **D7:** keep Sprint 0's base version (`v1.27.3-csci435-s0` → `v1.27.3-csci435-s1`), push the tag
  to origin, and write release notes listing the features, fixes and improvements.
- **Reviews:** each student reviews at least one PR per sprint. Over the semester, each student
  reviews every teammate at least once.
- **Extra credit:** up to 3 points per PR accepted by upstream Gitea.

## Branches and commits

- Branches: `feat/issue-<N>-short-description`, `fix/issue-<N>-short-description` or
  `chore/short-description` (`STUDENTS.md`). One issue per branch.
- Commit messages follow Conventional Commits and end with the issue number:
  `feat(repo): show empty state on releases page (#17)`. Add an
  `Assisted-by: AGENT_NAME:MODEL_VERSION` trailer when AI helped; never `Co-Authored-By` or
  `Signed-off-by` (`AGENTS.md`). A human approves every commit before it is made.

### Before each implementation: sync with main

Every new branch starts from an up-to-date `main`. AI sessions run this before writing any code:

```bash
git switch main
git pull origin main
git switch -c feat/issue-<N>-short-description
```

To pick up new work on `main` for a branch that already exists, **merge, don't rebase**. Rebasing
or squashing after review has started is not allowed (`docs/sprint0/standards.md`):

```bash
git fetch origin
git merge origin/main
```

Do this before opening the PR and again if `main` moves while it is in review. Never merge another
feature branch into yours.

### After merge: clean up

A PR is merged with a merge commit once it is approved, every review comment is addressed and CI
passes. Then:

```bash
git switch main
git pull origin main
git branch -d feat/issue-<N>-short-description               # local branch
git push origin --delete feat/issue-<N>-short-description    # or GitHub's "Delete branch" button
git fetch --prune                                            # drop stale remote-tracking refs
```

Also check that the issue closed (via `Closes #N`), is on the sprint milestone, and has its AI
Assistance comment. Then run `specstory sync` and file the session's log (see `ai-logs/README.md`).

<Version or commit, browser/OS, logs, screenshots.>
## Design Decision
<Same four fields as above: Decision, Alternatives Considered, Rationale, Consequences.>
```

- **Design Decision (D3):** fill it in once you've picked an approach, before opening the PR. Put
  a second decision under another `### Decision 2` heading. If a PR changes the decision, update
  the issue body.
- **Peer review (D2):** a teammate reads the spec and comments `Spec reviewed — <notes>` on the
  issue before implementation starts.

## Pull request format

Template: `.github/pull_request_template.md`. Title uses Conventional Commits, e.g.
`fix(issues): keep label filter after search`. Description sections:

1. `Closes #<N>`, which links the issue and closes it on merge.
2. **What changed:** the change in your own words.
3. **Why:** the problem, and which acceptance criteria (AC1…) it satisfies.
4. **How it was tested / Test strategy:** tests added or updated and why these ones. Name any
   change that can't be tested automatically and how it was checked by hand. Every behaviour change
   needs a new or updated test.
5. **CI / manual verification:** CI status, or the commands run and their results.
6. **Design:** one line pointing at the Design Decision in the issue, or a note on how it changed.
7. **AI assistance:** format in `AI-ASSISTANCE.md` §2, with **no log link**.

Per-PR grading (20 points): correctness against the acceptance criteria 6, test strategy with
explanation 5, description quality 4, CI or manual verification 3, review rubric posted 2.

## Code review rubric

The reviewer posts this as a **PR comment**, as well as the GitHub review itself. A copy-paste copy
is in `.github/code-review-rubric.md`, so keep the two in sync. Pull the branch and test it when you
can, say what you checked, and mark each point as required or optional
(`docs/community-governance.md`). Score each row against the issue's acceptance criteria. Anything
below 7 needs a note saying what would raise it.

```markdown
### Code Review — @reviewer-username

**Checked:** <what you ran or tried>

| Criterion | Score (1–10) | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Correctness — implements issue requirements | | |
| Test coverage — tests present and meaningful | | |
| Code quality — style, naming, no duplication | | |
| Documentation — comments and PR description clear | | |
| AI transparency — evidence of human verification if AI used | | |
| Overall — merge as-is? | | |
```

## Sprint report (D6) sections

`docs/sprint<N>/report.md`, following `docs/sprint0/report.md`:

- Team: names, GitHub usernames, project name, repository link.
- Sprint overview.
- Backlog: milestone link, plus a table of title, owner, points, scope and status.
- Requirements and design: when specs were done, what surprised you, design rationale.
- Completed issues: title, owner, PR link, author, reviewer, what changed.
- Test strategy, including untestable changes and why.
- AI tool usage per member: tools, session count, AI log folder link, and 2–3 sentences on lessons
  learned.
- Release: tag and release link.
- Risks and retrospective: what worked, what slowed the team down, Sprint 2 changes.
- Sprint 2 plan: initial ideas and carryover issues.
````

```text
# web_src/js — page features and how they get wired up

**Read when:** adding or changing browser behaviour on a page.
**Not here:** Vue components -> `frontend-vue-components.md`; styling -> `frontend-css.md`; the HTML -> `templates.md`.

## Responsibilities

| Directory | Owns |
| --- | --- |
| `features/` | one file per page or feature (`repo-issue.ts`, `repo-diff.ts`, `repo-code.ts`), plus `features/admin/` and `features/comp/` for shared widgets |
| `modules/` | cross-cutting infrastructure: `fetch.ts`, `init.ts`, `observer.ts`, `i18n.ts`, `toast.ts`, `tippy.ts`, `fomantic.ts`, `clipboard.ts`, `codeeditor/` |
| `utils/` | pure helpers with no DOM assumptions: `dom.ts`, `html.ts`, `url.ts`, `time.ts`, `color.ts`, `string.ts` |
| `markup/`, `render/` | enhancing already-rendered content (anchors, mermaid, math) |
| `webcomponents/` | custom elements such as `relative-time`, `overflow-menu`, `aria-menu` |

## Key files

| Path | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| `web_src/js/index.ts` | the entry point: imports fomantic and `../css/index.css`, then passes every `initXxx` to `callInitFunctions` |
| `web_src/js/modules/init.ts` | `callInitFunctions`, `InitPerformanceTracer` |
| `web_src/js/modules/observer.ts` | `registerGlobalInitFunc`, `registerGlobalEventFunc`, `registerGlobalSelectorFunc`, `initGlobalSelectorObserver` |
| `web_src/js/modules/fetch.ts` | `GET`, `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, `DELETE` |
| `web_src/js/utils/dom.ts` | `showElem`, `hideElem`, `toggleElem`, `queryElems`, `createElementFromHTML` |
| `web_src/js/modules/i18n.ts` | `trN` — the frontend side of the locale system |

## Conventions & invariants

**Two ways to wire a feature, and new code should prefer the second.**

1. *Page-load init:* export `initFoo()` from a `features/` file and add it to the array in
   `index.ts`. Every function in that array runs on **every** page, so it must find its elements
   and return immediately when they are absent.
2. *Declarative:* `registerGlobalInitFunc('initFoo', (el) => {...})` in the module, and
   `data-global-init="initFoo"` on the element in the template. For clicks,
   `registerGlobalEventFunc('click', 'onFoo', ...)` with `data-global-click="onFoo"`. This covers
   elements added to the DOM later and runs once per element (guarded by an internal
   `_giteaGlobalInited` flag), so re-adding a node does not re-initialise it.

`registerGlobalSelectorFunc(selector, handler)` also exists, but `observer.ts` marks it as "less
efficient and less maintainable" — it is for element types already spread across many pages, not
for new work.

- **Ordering rule:** every `registerGlobalInitFunc` must run *before* `initGlobalSelectorObserver`,
  which `index.ts` deliberately calls last. Registering after it throws.
- **One function per element.** `callGlobalInitFunc` in `observer.ts` looks the attribute up as a
  whole string, so `data-global-init` names exactly one function — space-separating two is an open
  TODO there, not a feature. To add behaviour to an element that already has one (the new-issue
  title in `templates/repo/issue/new_form.tmpl` carries `autoFocusEnd`), put the attribute on a
  wrapper and query for the inner element.
- Data fetching goes through the `fetch.ts` wrappers, never a raw `fetch`.
- Show and hide with `.tw-hidden` plus `showElem` / `hideElem` / `toggleElem`. In Vue use
  `v-if`/`v-show` instead (`frontend-vue-components.md`).
- Use `node.getAttribute`, not `node.dataset` (camel-casing surprises), and never bind
  user-provided data onto a DOM node.
- Custom DOM events are prefixed `ce-`, declared as an exported constant next to their emitter —
  see `EventEditorContentChanged` in `features/comp/EditorMarkdown.ts`.
- TypeScript, per `docs/guidelines-frontend.md`: `import type` for type-only imports,
  `@ts-expect-error` over `@ts-ignore`, `!` rather than `?.`/`??` when a value always exists, and
  `async` only on a function that actually awaits.
- One feature per file or directory; ids and classes are kebab-case with 2-3 feature keywords.

## Recipes

**Add behaviour to an element.** Register a global init func in the owning `features/` module and
put `data-global-init="yourFuncName"` on the element in its template. No change to `index.ts`.

**Add a whole-page feature.** New `features/<name>.ts` exporting `initName()`, an early return when
its root element is missing, then add the import and the array entry in `index.ts`.

**Profile a slow page.** Append `?_ui_performance_trace=1` to the URL to print per-init timings.
`index.ts` already logs an error when total init exceeds 500ms.

**Look up an issue by its number.** `matchIssue` (`utils/match.ts`) is the `#` list's search: a
number comes back first (`services/issue/suggestion.go` → `GetSuggestion`), and the current issue
is left out. Keyword matches are limited to the kinds the viewer may read
(`routers/web/repo/issue_suggestions.go`), but the match by number (`GetIssueByIndex`) is not, so a
viewer who can't read pull requests still gets one typed by its number. The duplicate close
reason's preview in `features/repo-issue-status-button.ts` uses it.

**Run one test file.** `pnpm exec vitest <path-filter>` (`testing.md`).

## Gotchas

- Forgetting the early return in a page-load init means that feature's cost is paid on every page
  in Gitea, which is what the 500ms warning is there to catch.
- Fomantic-UI (jQuery) is vendored and deprecated. Do not build new features on it, and do not mix
  it with Vue — Vue may use its CSS classes but not its JavaScript.
- Which menu to build on, Fomantic dropdown or `<aria-menu>` (`web_src/js/webcomponents/aria-menu.ts`),
  is decided in `web_src/js/modules/fomantic/aria.md`.
- `utils/` is for pure helpers. A function that reaches for `window` or a global selector belongs
  in `modules/` or `features/`.
- A feature can follow a comment box it did not create: the editor's change and upload events
  bubble (`features/comp/EditorMarkdown.ts`, `features/comp/EditorUpload.ts`), and
  `getComboMarkdownEditor` finds the editor, as `features/repo-issue-status-button.ts` does. But
  the editor attaches itself before its async `init` finishes, and calling it before then throws;
  read its textarea until an event arrives.
- Enter on a Fomantic dropdown item only fires a `click` when the item is a link or carries
  `js-aria-clickable` (`web_src/js/modules/fomantic/dropdown.ts`), so a plain click listener on other
  items never hears a keyboard pick. The close reason menu in `templates/repo/issue/view_content.tmpl`
  marks its items; an `<aria-menu>` item needs no class, as Enter and Space call its `click()`.
- After a click on a Fomantic dropdown item, the dropdown keeps the focus, so focusing something
  else from your click handler needs `setTimeout(..., 0)`.
- `createTippy` (`modules/tippy.ts`) moves a popup to `document.body`, so inputs in it leave their
  `<form>` and are not sent. Keep their values in hidden fields inside the form, as the close reason
  popups in `features/repo-issue-status-button.ts` do.

## Related

- `frontend-vue-components.md` — when a feature should be a Vue app instead
- `templates.md` — where `data-global-init` attributes and `pageData` come from
- `frontend-css.md` — `tw-hidden` and the class conventions
```

````text
# Background

This document is used as aria/accessibility(a11y) reference for future developers.

There are a lot of a11y problems in the Fomantic UI library. Files in
`web_src/js/modules/fomantic/` are used as a workaround to make the UI more accessible.

The aria-related code is designed to avoid touching the official Fomantic UI library,
and to be as independent as possible, so it can be easily modified/removed in the future.

To test the aria/accessibility with screen readers, developers can use the following steps:

* On macOS, you can use VoiceOver.
  * Press `Command + F5` to turn on VoiceOver.
  * Try to operate the UI with keyboard-only.
  * Use Tab/Shift+Tab to switch focus between elements.
  * Arrow keys (Option+Up/Down) to navigate between menu/combobox items (only aria-active, not really focused).
  * Press Enter to trigger the aria-active element.
* On Android, you can use TalkBack.
  * Go to Settings -> Accessibility -> TalkBack, turn it on.
  * Long-press or press+swipe to switch the aria-active element (not really focused).
  * Double-tap means old single-tap on the aria-active element.
  * Double-finger swipe means old single-finger swipe.
* TODO: on Windows, on Linux, on iOS

# Known Problems

* Tested with Apple VoiceOver: If a dropdown menu/combobox is opened by mouse click, then arrow keys don't work.
  But if the dropdown is opened by keyboard Tab, then arrow keys work, and from then on, the keys almost work with mouse click too.
  The clue: when the dropdown is only opened by mouse click, VoiceOver doesn't send 'keydown' events of arrow keys to the DOM,
  VoiceOver expects to use arrow keys to navigate between some elements, but it couldn't.
  Users could use Option+ArrowKeys to navigate between menu/combobox items or selection labels if the menu/combobox is opened by mouse click.

# Checkbox

## Accessibility-friendly Checkbox

The ideal checkboxes should be:

```html
<label><input type="checkbox"> ... </label>
```

However, the templates still have the Fomantic-style HTML layout:

```html
<div class="ui checkbox">
  <input type="checkbox">
  <label>...</label>
</div>
```

We call `initAriaLabels` to link the `input` and `label` which makes clicking the
label etc. work. There is still a problem: These checkboxes are not friendly to screen readers,
so we add IDs to all the Fomantic UI checkboxes automatically by JS. If the `label` part is empty,
then the checkbox needs to get the `aria-label` attribute manually.

# The `<aria-menu>` Web Component

New action menus (a button that opens a list of choices, with no search input and no selection state)
should use `<aria-menu>` from `web_src/js/webcomponents/aria-menu.ts` instead of a Fomantic dropdown.
It follows the ARIA menu button pattern and moves real focus onto the items (roving `tabindex`),
so the VoiceOver arrow key problem above cannot happen. Try it on the `/devtest/aria-menu` page.

```html
<aria-menu>
  <button type="button">Actions</button> <!-- first non-.menu child is the trigger -->
  <div class="menu">
    <a class="item" href="...">...</a>
    <div class="divider"></div>
    <div class="item">...</div> <!-- Enter, Space and click all fire the item's "click" -->
  </div>
</aria-menu>
```

The popup opens below the trigger, aligned to its start. Two optional host attributes, read only by CSS, move it:

* `placement="bottom-start|bottom-end|top-start|top-end"`, the same words as `data-tooltip-placement`.
  The template knows where the menu sits, so there is no automatic flip: a menu at the right edge needs `bottom-end`.
* `pointing` draws Fomantic's small arrow on a bottom placement.

Put `data-tooltip-content` on the trigger, not the host, so the tooltip text also becomes the trigger's `aria-label`.
The tooltip will not show while the menu is open.

Comboboxes, searchable and multiple-selection dropdowns still use Fomantic Dropdown below.

# Fomantic Dropdown

Fomantic Dropdown is designed to be used for many purposes:

* Menu (the theme menu in footer)
* Popup (the branch/tag panel, the review box)
* Simple `<select>` , used in many forms
* Searchable option-list with static items (used in many forms)
* Searchable option-list with dynamic items (ajax)
* Searchable multiple selection option-list with dynamic items: the repo topic setting
* More complex usages, like the Issue Label selector

Fomantic Dropdown requires that the focus must be on its primary element.
If the focus changes, it hides or panics.

At the moment, the aria-related code only tries to partially resolve the a11y problems for dropdowns with items.

There are different solutions:

* combobox + listbox + option:
  * https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/combobox/
  * A combobox is an input widget with an associated popup that enables users to select a value for the combobox from
    a collection of possible values. In some implementations, the popup presents allowed values, while in other implementations,
    the popup presents suggested values, and users may either select one of the suggestions or type a value.
* menu + menuitem:
  * https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/menubar/
  * A menu is a widget that offers a list of choices to the user, such as a set of actions or functions.

The current approach is: detect if the dropdown has an input,
if yes, it works like a combobox, otherwise it works like a menu.
Multiple selection dropdowns (`ui multiple ... dropdown`) are partially supported:

* the listbox has `aria-multiselectable="true"` and every option has `aria-selected`,
  refreshed after each add or remove (Fomantic marks the chosen items `active`)
* adding or removing an item is announced through the shared live region in
  `web_src/js/modules/aria-announce.ts`; Fomantic doesn't call `onAdd`/`onRemove` on the
  initial load, so existing selections are not read out
* a selection label's delete icon is named after the label's visible text
* picking an item keeps the keyboard focus: a `GITEA-PATCH` in `web_src/fomantic/build/components/dropdown.js`
  stops Fomantic's IE11 workaround from blurring the dropdown itself, and the global Enter
  quick-submit (`web_src/js/features/common-form.ts`) skips an Enter the dropdown already handled

Still not working: moving between selection labels with Left/Right is not announced, because
`aria-activedescendant` only ever points at menu items.

The issue sidebar's label, assignee, reviewer and project pickers are not Fomantic multiple
dropdowns: selection there is the `checked` class managed by
`web_src/js/features/repo-issue-sidebar-combolist.ts`, which keeps `aria-selected` and the
announcements in step itself. Their items sit in a nested `.scrolling.menu`, which the patch
also covers.

The Fomantic part of this is temporary by design: it goes away when these dropdowns move off
Fomantic (`<aria-menu>` above is for action menus only, so it is not their replacement), while the
sidebar part stays unless the sidebar itself is rewritten.

A dropdown whose trigger is only an icon (a kebab, a split button's caret) needs a localised
`aria-label` in its template, or a `data-tooltip-content`, which the patch copies into `aria-label`.
A `menu` takes no name from its content, so give one to a dropdown that only shows its current
value too, like the footer theme selector. The patch never makes up a name: outside
`RUN_MODE = prod` it logs a console warning for any dropdown with no name and no visible text.

Some important pages for dropdown testing:

* Home(dashboard) page, the "Theme" menu in footer.
* Create New Repo page, a lot of dropdowns as combobox.
* Collaborators page, the "permission" dropdown (the old behavior was not quite good, it just works).

```html
<!-- read-only dropdown -->
<div class="ui dropdown"> <!-- focused here, then it's not perfect to use aria-activedescendant to point to the menu item -->
  <input type="hidden" ...>
  <div class="text">Default</div>
  <div class="menu" tabindex="-1"> <!-- "transition hidden|visible" classes will be added by $.dropdown() and when the dropdown is working -->
    <div class="item active selected">Default</div>
    <div class="item">...</div>
  </div>
</div>

<!-- search input dropdown -->
<div class="ui dropdown">
  <input type="hidden" ...>
  <input class="search" autocomplete="off" tabindex="0"> <!-- focused here -->
  <div class="text"></div>
  <div class="menu" tabindex="-1"> <!-- "transition hidden|visible" classes will be added by $.dropdown() and when the dropdown is working -->
    <div class="item selected">...</div>
    <div class="item">...</div>
  </div>
</div>
```
````

```text
import {generateElemId, hideElem, showElem} from '../utils/dom.ts';

// A menu button following https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/menu-button/ with no Fomantic.
// Markup: <aria-menu><button type="button">label</button><div class="menu"><a class="item">...</a></div></aria-menu>
// Optional host attributes, read only by CSS: placement="bottom-start|bottom-end|top-start|top-end" (default bottom-start), pointing
// Items get real focus (roving tabindex) instead of aria-activedescendant, see web_src/js/modules/fomantic/aria.md
window.customElements.define('aria-menu', class extends HTMLElement {
  trigger!: HTMLElement;
  popup!: HTMLElement;
  inited = false;

  connectedCallback() {
    // in <head>-loaded components, the children are not parsed yet while the page is still loading
    if (document.readyState === 'loading') {
      document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', this.init, {once: true});
    } else {
      this.init();
    }
  }

  disconnectedCallback() {
    document.removeEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', this.init);
    if (this.inited) this.close(false); // also removes the outside click listener
  }

  init = () => {
    if (this.inited) return;
    const popup = this.querySelector<HTMLElement>(':scope > .menu');
    const trigger = Array.from(this.children).find((el) => el !== popup) as HTMLElement | undefined;
    if (!popup || !trigger) return;
    this.inited = true;
    this.popup = popup;
    this.trigger = trigger;

    if (trigger.tagName !== 'BUTTON') {
      trigger.setAttribute('role', 'button');
      trigger.tabIndex = 0;
    }
    if (!popup.id) popup.id = generateElemId('aria-menu-popup-');
    trigger.setAttribute('aria-haspopup', 'menu');
    trigger.setAttribute('aria-expanded', 'false');
    trigger.setAttribute('aria-controls', popup.id);
    popup.setAttribute('role', 'menu');
    if (!popup.hasAttribute('aria-label') && !popup.hasAttribute('aria-labelledby')) {
      if (!trigger.id) trigger.id = generateElemId('aria-menu-trigger-');
      popup.setAttribute('aria-labelledby', trigger.id); // keeps the menu's name once focus is on an item
    }
    hideElem(popup);
    this.updateItemRoles();

    trigger.addEventListener('click', () => this.isOpen() ? this.close(true) : this.open('first'));
    trigger.addEventListener('keydown', this.onTriggerKeyDown);
    trigger.addEventListener('keyup', this.preventSpaceClick);
    popup.addEventListener('keydown', this.onPopupKeyDown);
    popup.addEventListener('keyup', this.preventSpaceClick);
    popup.addEventListener('click', (e) => {
      // bubble phase, so the item's own click handlers have already run
      if ((e.target as Element).closest('[role="menuitem"]')) this.close(true);
    });
  };

  // items may be added after init, e.g. by a feature script, so refresh them on every open
  updateItemRoles() {
    for (const child of this.popup.children) {
      if (child.classList.contains('item')) {
        child.setAttribute('role', 'menuitem');
        child.setAttribute('tabindex', '-1');
      } else if (child.classList.contains('divider')) {
        child.setAttribute('role', 'separator');
      } else {
        child.setAttribute('role', 'none');
      }
    }
  }

  items(): HTMLElement[] {
    // hidden items can't take focus, so leaving them in would stall opening and arrow keys
    return Array.from(this.popup.querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>(':scope > [role="menuitem"]:not(.tw-hidden)'));
  }
```

```text
test('profile menu is operable by keyboard', async ({page}) => {
  await login(page);
  await page.goto('/');
  const trigger = page.getByRole('button', {name: 'Profile and Settings…'});
  const menu = page.getByRole('menu', {name: 'Profile and Settings…'});

  await trigger.focus();
  await page.keyboard.press('Enter');
  await expect(trigger).toHaveAttribute('aria-expanded', 'true');
  await expect(page.getByRole('menuitem', {name: 'Profile', exact: true})).toBeFocused();

  const menuBox = (await menu.boundingBox())!;
  expect(menuBox.x + menuBox.width).toBeLessThanOrEqual(page.viewportSize()!.width);

  await page.keyboard.press('End');
  await expect(page.getByRole('menuitem', {name: 'Sign Out'})).toBeFocused();
  await page.keyboard.press('Home');
  await expect(page.getByRole('menuitem', {name: 'Profile', exact: true})).toBeFocused();
  await page.keyboard.press('Escape');
  await expect(menu).toBeHidden();
  await expect(trigger).toBeFocused();

  await page.keyboard.press('ArrowDown');
  for (const name of ['Starred', 'Subscriptions', 'Settings']) {
    await page.keyboard.press('s');
    await expect(page.getByRole('menuitem', {name})).toBeFocused();
  }
  await page.keyboard.press('Enter');
  await expect(page).toHaveURL(/\/user\/settings$/);
  await assertNoJsError(page);
});
```

````text
# AI assistance disclosure — required format

Course rule, not an upstream Gitea one. Every contributor discloses their own AI use per issue,
**even when no AI was used**. Source: the course AI Log Instructions page and `CONTRIBUTING.md`
(AI Contribution Policy). Two separate places, both required. The rest of the PR and issue
format is in `COURSE-WORKFLOW.md`.

## 1. A comment on the issue

Posted by each contributor on the **issue** they worked, once their work is done. One comment per
person — never edit someone else's. Add later sessions by editing your own table.

```markdown
### AI Assistance — @your-github-username

**Role in this issue:** Implementation

| # | Tool | Log | What AI helped with |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | claude-code | [2026-09-24_claude-code_issue-52-impl.md](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/blob/main/ai-logs/sprint1/YourName/2026-09-24_claude-code_issue-52-impl.md) | Confirmed the files found during concept location, drafted the template change and tests, ran them |

**Attachments:** [2026-09-24_claude-code_issue-52-impl/](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/tree/main/ai-logs/sprint1/YourName/2026-09-24_claude-code_issue-52-impl)
```

- **Role** is one of Implementation, Code review, Testing, Other — pick the ones that apply and
  delete the rest, do not leave the slash list in place.
- **Tool** is the tool's name, e.g. `claude-code`, `claude-web`.
- **Log** is a full `https://github.com/...` link to the filed log. Relative paths break in issue
  comments. File naming is in `ai-logs/README.md`.
- **Attachments** only when the log has a companion folder; otherwise drop the line.
- **No AI used?** Keep the heading and role line and write `No AI used` in place of the table.

## 2. A short section in the pull request description — no log link

Reviewers read the PR, and the review rubric scores "AI transparency", so the PR says how AI was
used and how you verified it. It does **not** link or cite the AI log: from Sprint 1 on, logs are
referenced in **issue comments only**, never in PR descriptions or PR comments (Sprint 1 page, D5).

```markdown
## AI assistance

Claude Code (claude-opus-5) drafted the handler and tests following the existing register/delete
code; I reviewed every line, ran the tests, checked the page by hand, and can explain each change.
AI log: see the AI Assistance comment on the linked issue.
```

Name the model, say what AI did and what you did, and point at the issue comment for the log.

## Rules that make a disclosure wrong

- **Placeholders left in**: `@your-github-username` or the full `Implementation / Code review /
  Testing / Other` list means the comment was pasted unread.
- **A log link in a PR description or PR comment.** Log links live in the issue comment only.
- **A log link that 404s.** Until the log is merged to `main`, link the branch that holds it; switch
  to the `main` link once merged.
- **A log folder that is not your GitHub username** — `ai-logs/sprint1/jdonohue/` is wrong when the
  account is `Jack-Donohue`.
- **Claiming work AI did as your own, or the reverse.** The claim must match the log.
- **AI-written replies to reviewer questions on your own issue or PR.** `CONTRIBUTING.md` forbids it:
  the questions are for you.

## For AI agents drafting an issue or PR

Put section 2 in every PR description you draft, and draft the section 1 issue comment
separately, both filled in from the session you actually ran — never with placeholders. You may
draft the wording, but say plainly that the human must review and edit it before posting, and leave
the issue comment for them to post under their own account.
> Sub-issue of #25 · **P2 — only if capacity allows** · estimate **5 points** (medium) · blocked by #61

## User Story
As a screen reader user, I want the menus I hit on every single page — the profile menu, the
create-new menu, the language menu and the comment "..." menu — to be the accessible ones, so
that the most-used menus in Gitea stop being the least usable ones.

## User Scenario
A keyboard user Tabs along the top bar of the dashboard, reaches the avatar button, presses Enter,
arrows down to "Settings" and presses Enter. They scroll to the footer, Tab to the language menu,
open it the same way and pick a language. On an issue, they Tab to a comment's "..." button, open
it and choose "Copy link" — the same three keystrokes each time.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AC1: Given the signed-in navbar, then the profile menu and the create-new menu in
      `templates/base/head_navbar.tmpl` use the component from #61 and no longer carry the
      `ui dropdown` class or get patched by `dropdown.ts`.
- [ ] AC2: Given the footer, then the language menu in `templates/base/footer_content.tmpl` uses
      the component, and choosing a language still switches it — the click handler in
      `web_src/js/features/common-page.ts:27` still fires or is replaced by an equivalent.
- [ ] AC3: Given an issue comment, then the "..." menu in
      `templates/repo/issue/view_content/context_menu.tmpl` uses the component, and every item
      still works: copy link, copy source, quote reply, reference issue, edit and delete.
- [ ] AC4: Given each migrated menu, when opened with the keyboard, then all of AC1–AC6 of #61
      hold — arrows, Home/End, type-ahead, Escape-restores-focus and the ARIA attributes.
- [ ] AC5: Given each migrated menu, then its visual appearance on both the light and dark themes
      is unchanged from before the migration, verified by a before/after screenshot in the PR.
- [ ] AC6: Given the migrated menus, when the existing e2e suite runs, then it passes — including
      any test using `clickDropdownItem` from `tests/e2e/utils.ts` against a migrated menu, which
      must either keep working or be updated in this PR.
- [ ] AC7: Playwright tests cover keyboard operation of the profile menu and the comment "..."
      menu end to end.

## Out of Scope
- The theme selector (`#footer-theme-selector`), whose menu is populated separately and is better
  migrated with the other JS-populated menus.
- Every dropdown that is a combobox, has a search input, or allows multiple selection — the issue
  sidebar label, assignee, reviewer, milestone and project menus all stay on Fomantic.
- The repository branch and tag selector.
- Deleting any part of `dropdown.ts`; it still serves the ~55 dropdowns left behind.

## Open Questions
- Does anything outside the repo rely on the `.ui.dropdown` class on the navbar items for custom
  CSS? Gitea supports custom templates and stylesheets, so this may be a note-worthy change for
  the release notes.

## Design Decision
**Decision:** Migrate only menus that are static, server-rendered and single-select, and keep the
existing Fomantic CSS class names on the new markup so the visual result is identical.

**Alternatives Considered:** (a) Migrate every `ui dropdown` in `templates/` in one PR.
(b) Migrate the same three menus but also write fresh CSS for them instead of reusing the Fomantic
classes.

**Rationale:** (a) is 61 occurrences spanning comboboxes, AJAX-populated lists and the label
multi-select — far past a sprint, and it would put untested changes on the issue sidebar, the most
complex dropdown in the product. The three chosen menus are the highest-traffic and the simplest,
so they give the most user benefit per unit of risk. On (b): reusing the class names keeps this PR
a behaviour change rather than a behaviour-plus-appearance change, which makes AC5 a screenshot
comparison instead of a design review, and keeps the diff reviewable.

**Consequences:** Easier — a reviewer can check the diff against one criterion, "does it still
look and behave the same", and the remaining dropdowns are untouched so nothing else can regress.
Harder — the new component inherits Fomantic's CSS class names and therefore its stylesheet, so
Fomantic's CSS cannot be dropped even after every menu is migrated; that cleanup becomes a
separate, later issue and should be recorded as such in #25.

## Scope
````

```markdown
Title: Move the Code tab, branch list and commit page action menus to <aria-menu>

Labels: enhancement, scope: medium · Milestone: Sprint 2

> Sub-issue of #25 · estimate **5 points** (medium) · no blockers: `<aria-menu>` (#61) is on `main`, and #62 is the pattern to follow

## User Story
As a keyboard or screen reader user browsing a repository's code, I want the "Add file", "More operations", branch download and commit "Operations" menus to behave like the navbar menus, so that I can add files, download archives and branch or tag from a commit without a mouse.

## User Scenario
A screen reader user opens a folder in `octo/app`. They Tab to **Add file**, press Enter, hear "Add file, menu", arrow down to "Upload file" and press Enter. Back in the folder, they open the "..." menu, press End to reach "Delete this directory" and Escape to close it, and focus returns to the "..." button. On the Branches page they open a branch's download menu and pick "TAR.GZ". On a commit page they open **Operations** and choose "Create tag", and the create-tag dialog opens.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AC1: Given the Code tab, when it renders, then the **Add file** menu and the folder **More operations** menu in `templates/repo/view_content.tmpl` are `<aria-menu>` elements, and neither has the `ui dropdown` class.
- [ ] AC2: Given the Branches page, when it renders, then the download menus for the default branch and for each other branch in `templates/repo/branch/list.tmpl` are `<aria-menu>`, and each trigger's name is its localised "Download …" tooltip text.
- [ ] AC3: Given a commit page and a user with write access to code, when it renders, then the **Operations** menu in `templates/repo/commit_page.tmpl` is an `<aria-menu>`. Its create branch, create tag, revert and cherry-pick items each open the same modal as before when picked with Enter or with a mouse click.
- [ ] AC4: Given each migrated menu, when operated by keyboard, then Enter/Space/ArrowDown opens it with focus on the first item, ArrowUp/ArrowDown/Home/End move focus, Escape closes it and returns focus to the trigger, and the trigger's `aria-expanded` matches the menu's visibility.
- [ ] AC5: Given each item, when picked with the keyboard, then it does what a mouse click did before: copy permalink copies the URL, ZIP/TAR.GZ start the archive download through `archive-link`, and links navigate.
- [ ] AC6: Given a repository where the web editor can't be enabled, when the Code tab renders, then the **Add file** trigger is still disabled and its menu can't be opened.
- [ ] AC7: Given light and dark themes, when the migrated menus are compared before and after, then their position and look are the same. The PR includes before/after screenshots.
- [ ] AC8: Playwright tests in `tests/e2e/` open the Add file menu, the folder menu and the commit Operations menu by keyboard and pick an item from each. The existing e2e and Go integration suites still pass.

## Out of Scope
- The branch/tag selector (`templates/repo/branch_dropdown.tmpl`) and the clone panel: they are searchable popups, not action menus.
- The file view's own toolbar menus, and the diff options menu (`templates/repo/diff/options_dropdown.tmpl`). They are possible follow-ups under #25.
- Any change to what the menus contain or to who can see them.

## Open Questions
- The commit **Operations** menu repeats its own name as a `.header` row inside the menu. Keep it (it gets `role="none"`) or drop it now that the menu is named after its trigger? (Proposed: drop it, as screen readers would read the name twice.)
- Should the folder menu use `placement="bottom-end"`, since it sits near the right edge on narrow screens?

## Design Decision
### Decision 1: which component to move to
**Decision:** Rebuild each menu as an `<aria-menu>` with a `<button type="button">` trigger and a sibling `.menu`, following `web_src/js/modules/fomantic/aria.md` and #62.

**Alternatives Considered:**
- (a) Keep the Fomantic dropdowns and extend the ARIA patch in `web_src/js/modules/fomantic/dropdown.ts`.
- (b) Write a small Vue component for these menus.

**Rationale:** (a) can't fix the VoiceOver arrow key problem listed under "Known Problems" in `aria.md`. Fomantic keeps focus on the trigger and fakes item focus with `aria-activedescendant`, while `<aria-menu>` moves real focus. Upstream also plans to drop Fomantic (go-gitea/gitea#29849). (b) would mount a Vue app just to show a few server-rendered links. `frontend-js.md` keeps Vue for whole interactive views, and `aria.md` already names `<aria-menu>` as the component for new action menus.

**Consequences:** Easier: these menus get the same keyboard behaviour and tests as the navbar, and `dropdown.ts` handles four fewer menus. Harder: today the Add file and folder menus put `.menu` *inside* a `<button>`, which is invalid HTML. The trigger and the menu have to be split into siblings, so any custom CSS that targets `button.repo-add-file .menu` will stop matching.

### Decision 2: how items keep working
**Decision:** Keep every item's existing classes and data attributes (`archive-link`, `show-create-branch-modal`, `show-modal`, `data-clipboard-text`) and let `<aria-menu>` call `click()` on Enter/Space. No item handler changes.

**Alternatives Considered:**
- (a) Rewrite the item handlers to listen for `<aria-menu>` events.
- (b) Turn every item into an `<a href>` so Enter works natively.

**Rationale:** The handlers are delegated from `document` (`common-button.ts`) or bound at page load (`repo-branch.ts`, `repo-common.ts`), so they still fire when the item moves into an `<aria-menu>`. (a) would change working code for no gain. (b) can't work for items that open modals and have no URL.

**Consequences:** Easier: the diff is only template changes and tests. Harder: `repo-branch.ts` binds `.show-create-branch-modal` with `querySelectorAll` at load, so an item added later wouldn't work. That's fine today, but it should be noted in the PR's Tech Debt section.

## Scope
medium (5 points)
```

```markdown
Title: Move the "…" row menus on the Actions, Projects and Packages pages to <aria-menu>, with disabled items

Labels: enhancement, scope: medium · Milestone: Sprint 2

> Sub-issue of #25 · estimate **5 points** (medium) · no blockers: `<aria-menu>` (#61) is on `main`

## User Story
As a keyboard or screen reader user managing a repository, I want the "…" menus on workflow runs, workflows, project columns and package cleanup rules to be operable from the keyboard, so that I can cancel a run, disable a workflow or edit a column without a mouse.

## User Scenario
A maintainer using a screen reader opens the Actions tab. They Tab to a running job's "…" button and hear "More operations, menu button, collapsed". They press Enter, arrow to "Cancel" and press Enter, and the run is cancelled. They open the workflow's "…" menu, where "Disable workflow" is announced as "dimmed" because the workflow is required, so pressing Enter on it does nothing. On a project board they open a column's "…" menu and choose "Edit", and the edit dialog opens.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AC1: Given the Actions tab, when it renders, then the workflow "…" menu (`templates/repo/actions/list.tmpl`) and every run row's "…" menu (`templates/repo/actions/runs_list.tmpl`) are `<aria-menu>` elements with no `ui dropdown` class, and each trigger is named "More operations".
- [ ] AC2: Given a project board and a user with write access, when it renders, then each column's "…" menu (`templates/projects/view.tmpl`) is an `<aria-menu>`. Edit opens the column modal, and "Set as default" and "Delete" show their confirmation dialogs, by keyboard and by mouse.
- [ ] AC3: Given a package cleanup rule list, when it renders, then each rule's "…" menu (`templates/package/shared/cleanup_rules/list.tmpl`) is an `<aria-menu>`, and "Edit" and "Preview" navigate.
- [ ] AC4: Given a menu item with the `disabled` class, when the menu is open, then the item has `aria-disabled="true"`, arrow keys still reach it, and Enter, Space or a click on it does nothing and leaves the menu open.
- [ ] AC5: Given a required workflow, when its "…" menu is opened, then "Disable workflow" is disabled as in AC4. For a workflow that isn't required, it sends the same enable/disable request as today.
- [ ] AC6: Given each migrated menu, when operated by keyboard, then Enter/Space/ArrowDown opens it with focus on the first item, Home/End and the arrows move focus, and Escape closes it and returns focus to the trigger.
- [ ] AC7: Given a project board, when a column's "…" menu is opened or used by keyboard, then the column is not picked up or moved by the board's drag-and-drop.
- [ ] AC8: A Vitest test in `web_src/js/webcomponents/aria-menu.test.ts` covers AC4. Playwright tests cover cancelling a run and opening a column's Edit dialog by keyboard. The existing suites still pass.

## Out of Scope
- The "Create new runner" menu (`templates/shared/actions/runner_list.tmpl`): it holds a text input and a copy button, so it is a popup, not a menu.
- The Actions page filter menus (actor, status, branch): they show a current selection, so they stay Fomantic like the other filters.
- The run page's own re-run menu in `web_src/js/components/RepoActionView.vue`.

## Open Questions
- Should a disabled item also say *why* it is disabled (for example "required by organisation settings")? (Proposed: not in this issue. Today the menu shows no reason either.)
- Should the run row menus use `placement="bottom-end"`, since they sit at the right edge of each row?

## Design Decision
### Decision 1: which component to move to
**Decision:** Rebuild the four menus as `<aria-menu>` and keep every item's `link-action`, `show-modal` and `data-modal-confirm` attributes, as #62 did for the comment menu.

**Alternatives Considered:**
- (a) Keep the Fomantic dropdowns and extend the ARIA patch in `web_src/js/modules/fomantic/dropdown.ts`.
- (b) Move only the Actions menus and leave Projects and Packages for later.

**Rationale:** (a) can't fix the VoiceOver arrow key problem in `aria.md`, and upstream is removing Fomantic (go-gitea/gitea#29849). (b) would leave the same "…" menu working two different ways depending on the page. All four share one markup shape and the delegated `link-action`/`show-modal` handlers, so the extra two cost little.

**Consequences:** Easier: every "…" row menu outside the issue sidebar behaves the same, and `dropdown.ts` handles four fewer menu types. Harder: a run list can render many `<aria-menu>` elements per page, each with its own listeners. That's fine at 20–50 rows, but if the list ever grows unpaginated, a single delegated menu would scale better.

### Decision 2: how disabled items work
**Decision:** Teach `<aria-menu>` to mark `.item.disabled` children `aria-disabled="true"` in `updateItemRoles`. They stay focusable but don't activate, and the menu stays open on Enter, Space or click.

**Alternatives Considered:**
- (a) Leave disabled items out of the menu when the workflow is required.
- (b) Skip disabled items when moving with the arrow keys.

**Rationale:** The WAI-ARIA menu pattern keeps disabled items focusable so screen reader users learn the option exists. (a) hides that, and it changes what sighted users see. (b) matches neither the APG nor native OS menus, and a user who can only reach an item by pointer would never hear about it.

**Consequences:** Easier: any later menu with a disabled item works without extra code. Harder: this changes the shared component, so the navbar and comment menus from #62 must be re-checked. The existing `aria-menu.test.ts` and `tests/e2e/menus.test.ts` cover them.

## Scope
medium (5 points)
```

```markdown
Title: Move the "Add webhook", "Link account" and admin notice "Operations" menus to <aria-menu>

Labels: enhancement, scope: medium · Milestone: Sprint 2

> Sub-issue of #25 · estimate **5 points** (medium) · no blockers: `<aria-menu>` (#61) is on `main`

## User Story
As a keyboard or screen reader user configuring a repository, organisation, account or the site, I want the menus that add a webhook, link an external account or act on admin notices to be operable from the keyboard, so that settings pages don't block me in the places I configure integrations.

## User Scenario
An organisation owner using a screen reader opens **Settings → Webhooks**. They Tab to **Add webhook**, press Enter, type "s" twice to move from "Slack" to the next item starting with "s", and press Enter to open the new webhook form. On that form the type switcher at the top is read as "Webhook type: Slack, menu button", and they use it to switch to "Discord". Later they open **Settings → Security**, open **Link account** and choose a sign-in provider. A site admin opens **Site administration → System notices**, opens **Operations** above the table and picks "Select all".

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AC1: Given the webhook list on the repository, organisation, user and admin settings pages (all rendered by `templates/repo/settings/webhook/base_list.tmpl`), when it renders, then **Add webhook** is an `<aria-menu>` whose items are the links from `templates/repo/settings/webhook/link_menu.tmpl`, and it has no `ui dropdown` class.
- [ ] AC2: Given the new webhook form (`templates/webhook/new.tmpl`), when it renders, then the type switcher is an `<aria-menu>`. Its trigger is named with both a localised "webhook type" label and the current type, not the type name alone.
- [ ] AC3: Given at least one OAuth2 sign-in source, when **Settings → Security** renders, then the **Link account** menu (`templates/user/settings/security/accountlinks.tmpl`) is an `<aria-menu>` and each provider item navigates to its `/user/oauth2/<name>` URL.
- [ ] AC4: Given **Site administration → System notices**, when it renders, then the **Operations** menu (`templates/admin/notice.tmpl`) is an `<aria-menu>` that opens upwards (`placement="top-start"`). "Select all", "Deselect all" and "Inverse selection" change the table checkboxes by keyboard and by mouse.
- [ ] AC5: Given each migrated menu, when operated by keyboard, then Enter/Space/ArrowDown opens it with focus on the first item, the arrows, Home/End and first-letter type-ahead move focus, and Escape closes it and returns focus to the trigger.
- [ ] AC6: Given light and dark themes, when the migrated menus are compared before and after, then their position and look are the same, including the webhook icons. The PR includes before/after screenshots.
- [ ] AC7: Playwright tests cover adding a webhook from the repository settings page and switching the webhook type, both by keyboard. The existing e2e and Go integration suites still pass.

## Out of Scope
- Webhook form fields themselves (the content type and HTTP method `<select>`s and the events checkboxes).
- The admin list filter menus ("Sort", "Filter") in `templates/admin/*/list.tmpl`: they show a current selection, so they stay Fomantic like the other filters.
- Adding new webhook types or providers.

## Open Questions
- Is a new locale key needed for the AC2 label, or can an existing key such as `repo.settings.webhook.type` be reused? (A new key goes into `options/locale/locale_en-US.ini` only.)
- `link_menu.tmpl` lists about 15 webhook types. Should type-ahead be the only shortcut, or should the menu scroll with a maximum height?

## Design Decision
### Decision 1: where to make the change
**Decision:** Change the two templates that wrap `link_menu.tmpl` (`base_list.tmpl` and `webhook/new.tmpl`), not each settings page. That one change covers the repository, organisation, user and admin webhook pages.

**Alternatives Considered:**
- (a) Change each settings page's template separately.
- (b) Leave the webhook menus on Fomantic and add only the missing names through the existing ARIA patch.

**Rationale:** All four pages already include `base_list.tmpl`, so (a) would copy the same markup four times and risk the copies drifting apart. (b) leaves the VoiceOver arrow key problem in `aria.md` unfixed. Upstream is also removing Fomantic (go-gitea/gitea#29849).

**Consequences:** Easier: one template change, one e2e test on the repository page, and the other three pages are covered by sharing the markup. Harder: `link_menu.tmpl` must keep its outer `.menu` element to be a valid `<aria-menu>` child, so it can't be reused as a plain list anywhere else without that wrapper.

### Decision 2: naming the type switcher
**Decision:** Give the new webhook form's type switcher an `aria-label` that combines a "webhook type" label with the current type.

**Alternatives Considered:**
- (a) Let the trigger take its name from its visible text, the current type alone.
- (b) Add a visible "Type:" text label next to the switcher.

**Rationale:** `aria.md` says a menu that only shows its current value needs a name of its own. "Slack, menu button" doesn't tell the user that the button switches the type. (b) also fixes that, but it changes the page's look, which AC6 rules out for this issue.

**Consequences:** Easier: the trigger is clear to screen readers and nothing changes visually. Harder: the label can fall out of sync with the visible text if someone later changes one and not the other, so the template should build both from the same `HookType` value.

## Scope
medium (5 points)
```

````text
# Mid-Sprint Check-in: @controlled-opposition

## Question 1: What did you implement so far in the sprint, and what remains?

I've implemented #65, the Playwright regression suite for dropdowns. The tests check that the issue label picker and the navbar menus set `aria-expanded` and the related ARIA attributes correctly as they open and close. PR #105 is open and waiting for a teammate review. While writing these tests I found a real bug: the label picker keeps `aria-expanded="true"` after Escape closes it. I filed it as #104 and marked that test with `test.fail()` so the suite stays green until the bug is fixed.

Three issues remain. #57 (medium) adds a `?` shortcut that opens a help dialog listing every registered shortcut. #95 (small) makes `r` quote the selected text into the reply box. #60 (small) lets users turn character-key shortcuts off, following WCAG 2.1.4. All three build on the shortcut registry from #56, which merged on 10-19. I'll do #57 first because #60 depends on it, and my UML diagrams will cover #57.

## Question 2: What is one thing you learned about the codebase or about software engineering practice?

Writing tests against what the user can observe found a bug that the existing tests had missed. Screen readers rely on the label picker's `aria-expanded` attribute, and no test checked it after Escape. The picker looked closed on screen but still reported itself as open. A test that only checked visibility would have passed. From now on, when I test an interactive widget, I'll assert the attributes assistive technology reads as well as what appears on screen.

I also learned how to keep a known bug from blocking work. If I'd left the failing assertion in place, CI would have gone red for everyone until someone fixed #104. If I'd deleted it, the bug would have been forgotten. `test.fail()` records the bug in the suite and leaves the build passing. When someone fixes #104, that test will start to fail, and that tells them to remove the marker. The bug stays documented and has a check waiting for the fix.

## Question 3: What is one thing you would do differently?

I would start the dependent issues earlier. I picked up #57, #60 and #95 on 10-18, and all three depended on #56, which hadn't merged yet. I waited for that merge instead of starting work, so halfway through the sprint I have one PR open and three issues with no code. I could have branched off the #56 branch and rebased once it merged, or started with the parts that don't touch the registry, such as the help dialog's markup or the text-selection logic for `r`.

I'd also install fewer skills in my AI setup. Every skill I add puts its name and description into the agent's context at the start of each session, so dozens of them use up context before I've asked for anything. Having so many also confuses the agent. Several skills overlap, so it sometimes loads one that doesn't fit the task, or follows instructions from two skills that disagree. I'm going to go through my skills, remove the ones I rarely use, and keep a short list that matches how I work on this project.

# AI Logs

This folder holds every AI session for each sprint, one folder per student. The course rules are on
the [AI Log Instructions](https://csci-435-se.github.io/ai-logs/) page and the current sprint page
at <https://csci-435-se.github.io/>. This README is the team's shared convention for following them.

## What to log

Every AI session tied to this project: code, debugging, tests, reviews, drafting issues and PRs,
design discussion, the sprint report. That includes sessions that went nowhere. Purely academic
questions unrelated to the project don't need logging.

## Structure

```
ai-logs/
  sprint1/
    <github-username>/                          ← exact GitHub username, matching case
      .gitkeep                                  ← the folder must exist even if you used no AI
      YYYY-MM-DD_<tool>_<short-slug>.md
      YYYY-MM-DD_<tool>_<short-slug>/           ← attachments (images, etc.), optional
```

Team folders: `ab-wm`, `arjunsb26`, `CarsonRackley`, `controlled-opposition`, `Jack-Donohue`,
`vvchopra`.

## Naming

`YYYY-MM-DD_<tool>_<short-slug>.md`

- **Date:** the day the session started.
- **Sprint folder:** the sprint that date falls in, not the sprint the work is for.
- **Tool:** one of the course identifiers: `claude-code`, `claude-web`, `claude-desktop`, `cursor`,
  `gemini-cli`, `codex-cli`, `copilot`, `chatgpt`, `other-<name>`. Claude Code run inside VS Code is
  `claude-code`.
- **Slug:** lowercase words joined with hyphens that say what the session did. Put the issue number
  first when there is one: `issue-52-impl`, `issue-52-spec`, `pr-61-review`, `sprint1-report`.
  Replace auto-generated slugs such as `local-command-caveat...`.
- **Formats:** `.md` is preferred; `.txt` and `.json` are also accepted. No `.docx`, `.pdf`, `.html`
  or share links.

## Capturing a session

| Tool | How |
| --- | --- |
| Claude Code (terminal or VS Code), other agentic CLIs | Start it with [SpecStory](https://specstory.com/): `specstory run claude`, from the repo root. Forgot? Run `specstory sync` afterwards; it back-fills from Claude Code's local history. Then copy from `.specstory/history/` (git-ignored) into your folder and rename it to the convention. |
| Web chat (claude.ai, ChatGPT, Gemini, ...) | Install a browser chat exporter and export the session as Markdown right after it ends. Include any files you pasted in as context. |
| Claude Desktop | SpecStory doesn't capture it. Copy the conversation into a `.md` file by hand. |

At the end of each sprint, run `specstory sync` once more and re-copy. A log copied mid-session is
incomplete.

## Content

- The **tool and AI model** used (SpecStory writes both).
- The **complete** prompt and response history. For agentic tools, that includes file edits and
  commands (SpecStory includes them). Logs with missing responses or truncated histories are
  **invalid**. Don't hand-write, summarise or trim a log; only rename it.
- Attachments (screenshots, snippets) go in a folder with the log's name minus `.md`.
- Log **every** session, including ones that went nowhere. Grading is on how complete the record
````

```markdown
# Mid-Sprint Check-in: @Jack-Donohue

## Question 1: What did you implement so far in the sprint, and what remains?
```

So far, within this sprint, I have not made any implementations; unfortunately, for most of this month I have no memories at all, so even what has become of sprint one is mostly a mystery to me. Apropos Wednesday, I can state with certainty that I slept 15 hours, and for much of the time before that the days passed in similar smarting sloth. I can say that for at least the nary too distant days I have worked on the slides for our presentation of the first sprint and on deploying Claude to generate new issues, as we are unfortunately short on the list of medium issues to labor on. A particular number of these newly fabricated issues are prescient to the commission performed within the first and current sprints, which is certainly tightening the noose around our work pace with such extensive dependency shackles, but I cannot expect Claude to be very creative in terms of discovering contemporary feature requests unless we resort to plagiarizing the original repo's issues.

## Question 2: What is one thing you learned about the codebase or about software engineering practice?

While generally covered in existing material as part of a course on project management I first had to undertake as the final section of my Bachelor's, it is beneficial to have specific coverage of management and good practices that have been created by those that have come before me specifically for the field of digital software design. While the separation of individual elements of software into modules is not unexplored territory, the specific language and division of these concepts into coupling & cohesion is something I have been recently trying to find words to express and explore on other projects. Modular design is useful for human use of course, as it assists in the creation of systems that can be mentally divided and in some aspects expected to work independently of each other, something important for collaborative creation or monolithic systems; but as we progress further into the use of agentic tools for the creation of systems, it is critical: it gives us the ability to deploy multiple agents, reduces the context drift and the costs of feeding them a lot of information, and provides some protection by restricting the impact of a bad change.

## Question 3: What is one thing you would do differently?

I would like to say that I would be less sleepy and more on top of tasks, but as I write this I am struggling to stay awake even after a normal person's amount of sleep and a lot of caffeine. Going forward, I would like to take more initiative in providing information to Claude and in a more thorough interrogation of its ideas as we are getting further into the development of issues on the Gitea platform; however, it remains, as ever, very complicated. Overall, on both the sprint and the documentation I have been one of the last to contribute, which I would like to change; though in this sprint's first half I spent most of my time debating withdrawal from the class, as there was nothing graded and I had begun to expect that nothing would be graded until the very last sprint, so I hesitated to pick up an issue just to leave it incomplete.
